title: Inferring Off-Target Effects of Drugs on Cellular Signaling Using Deep Learning
author: Meimetis, Lauffenburger, et al.

steps.title: Install software and download data
steps.instruction: Install all required software packages for DT‑LEMBAS and download the pre‑compiled drug‑target interaction files, L1000 transcriptomic data, and any other resources referenced in the GitHub repository (https://github.com/Lauffenburger-Lab/DrugsANNSignaling).

steps.title: Prepare drug concentration matrix
steps.instruction: Create the input file “DrugsIn” in tab‑separated (.tsv) format containing log‑transformed drug concentrations; rows correspond to samples (experimental conditions) and columns to the available drugs. Curate this file manually.

steps.title: Generate drug‑target interaction file
steps.instruction: Retrieve pre‑compiled drug‑target interactions (DTIs) or compile your own using the same file format; save as “TargetsIn” (.tsv) with drugs as rows and target proteins as columns. This file will be used in the modeling pipeline.

steps.title: Infer transcription factor activities
steps.instruction: Apply the DoRothEA regulon together with the VIPER algorithm to the L1000 gene‑expression data to infer TF activity, then preprocess and filter TFs and samples as needed; export the resulting activity matrix as “TFsOut” (.tsv).

steps.title: Build prior knowledge network
steps.instruction: Construct a prior knowledge signaling network (PKN) containing approximately 12 000 interactions and save it as the “PKN” file; also generate the corresponding annotation file “PknAnnotation”. The PKN will serve as the scaffold for the recurrent neural‑network component of DT‑LEMBAS.

steps.title: Train cell‑line specific models
steps.instruction: Using the prepared “DrugsIn”, “TargetsIn”, “TFsOut”, and “PKN” files, train DT‑LEMBAS models for the chosen cell line (e.g., A375). For the example, train an ensemble of 50 independent models on the L1000 data; ensure the training set includes at least ~120 experimental conditions, ~100 TFs, and the ~12 k‑interaction PKN.

steps.title: Extract inferred DTIs and chemical similarities
steps.instruction: After training, extract the learned drug‑target interaction weights from each model and combine them to produce a matrix of inferred DTIs; compute pairwise chemical similarity between drugs and save the result as the “ChemicalSims” (.csv) matrix.

steps.title: Estimate off‑target effects on TFs
steps.instruction: Use the inferred DTIs to predict off‑target effects of each drug on specific transcription factors; select a TF of interest (e.g., FOXM1) and a drug (e.g., Lestaurtinib) for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Derive mechanism‑of‑action network
steps.instruction: From the off‑target predictions, extract a sub‑network of the PKN that connects the selected drug to the chosen TF, yielding a compact signaling network that explains the drug’s off‑target effect (e.g., Lestaurtinib → FOXM1).
